airExpress.name: Air Express
airExpress.description: The shortest available air schedule for urgent documents and parcels. The route and collection time are confirmed before acceptance.

airEconomy.name: Air Economy
airEconomy.description: A flexible air schedule for goods that do not need the fastest uplift. Suitable when cost matters more than a fixed arrival day.

oceanFreight.name: Ocean Freight (LCL)
oceanFreight.transitLabel: Schedule-based - exact sailing and transit shown at quote time
oceanFreight.description: Consolidated sea freight for cargo that is too heavy or bulky for economical air transport. Cut-off, sailing and destination charges are confirmed for the route.

ServicesPage.heroTitle: Choose a service after looking at the cargo.
ServicesPage.heroSubtitle: Speed is only one part of the decision. Weight, dimensions, route, handling and customs requirements determine which movement is practical.
ServicesPage.pricingNote: The final rate depends on chargeable weight, route and handling.
ServicesPage.compareSubheading: Use this as a routing guide. The available carrier schedule is confirmed against the actual shipment.
ServicesPage.pricingDisclaimer: Transit times begin after export acceptance and are not guarantees. Customs, weather, carrier changes and local delivery can affect arrival.
ServicesPage.needHelpBody: Send the route, contents, weight and dimensions. We will identify the practical options and tell you what still needs checking.

TrackingPage.trackingFormatHint: Nauterio tracking numbers start with NT and end with the destination-country code. Copy the complete number, including hyphens.

QuotePage.heroSubtitle: Enter the cargo and route. Any price shown here is a working estimate; Nauterio confirms the final rate and collection plan before accepting the shipment.
QuotePage.volumetricNote: Airlines charge based on the greater of actual weight or volumetric weight. Your chargeable weight will be <bold>{weight} kg</bold>.
QuotePage.protectionOptionBody: Optional. The estimate will show the charge; cover applies only if its terms are included in the approved shipment documents.
QuotePage.customRouteHeading: This route needs a custom review

CustomsPage.heroTitle: Customs starts with an accurate description.
CustomsPage.heroSubtitle: The rules depend on the goods, their origin and their destination. Give us the details before collection so we can identify missing documents or route restrictions.
CustomsPage.routeWarning: These lists are a starting point, not customs approval. A common item can still be restricted by a destination authority, airline, ocean carrier or import licence requirement.
CustomsPage.prohibitedDesc: These goods are frequently prohibited or tightly controlled. We may refuse them even where a permit exists.
prohibitedItems: Live plants, seeds and untreated soil
CustomsPage.restrictedDesc: These goods commonly need permits, specialist packaging, carrier approval or extra documents.
CustomsPage.allowedDesc: These goods are often accepted when correctly described and packed, but they are still checked against the route rules.
CustomsPage.documentationSubheading: Accurate paperwork matters more than paperwork that merely looks complete.
CustomsPage.invoiceIntro: For goods, describe the transaction and each item clearly:
CustomsPage.waybillIntro: The confirmed shipment record should match the cargo handed over:
CustomsPage.estimatorHeading: Import duty is not a flat percentage.
CustomsPage.estimatorSubheading: Duty and tax depend on the destination, commodity code, country of origin, declared value and the authority's decision. We do not present a generic percentage as a reliable landed cost.
CustomsPage.estimatorDisclaimer: The destination authority makes the final decision. For a binding classification or complex import, obtain advice from a qualified customs broker.

BusinessPage.heroTitle: A shipping process your team can repeat.
BusinessPage.heroSubtitle: If you ship every week or every month, send us the lanes, cargo and expected volume. We will discuss a workable collection plan, documentation process and account rate instead of forcing you into a generic package.
BusinessPage.whyChooseHeading: Built around the way your goods actually move
BusinessPage.whyChooseSubheading: Business arrangements are agreed from the real route and workload. There are no artificial tiers or features promised before they are needed.

workingPoints.title: Route planning
workingPoints.body: We review the regular origins, destinations, cargo profile and collection constraints before proposing a service.

workingPoints.title: Shared records
workingPoints.body: Quotes, shipment details, documents, invoices and milestone updates stay attached to the same customer account.

workingPoints.title: Exception handling
workingPoints.body: When customs, a carrier or the consignee needs something, the request is recorded against the shipment so the right person can act.

BusinessPage.enquiryHeading: Send the details that affect the operation
BusinessPage.enquiryBody: A good rate starts with a clear picture of the work. Estimates can be discussed before every detail is final, but the route and cargo cannot be guessed.
enquiryPoints: Usual origin and destination countries or cities
Typical contents, weight, dimensions and declared value
Expected number of shipments and seasonal peaks
Collection hours, delivery constraints and customs responsibilities
BusinessPage.customsDataBody: Commercial invoice and HS code guidance is built into the booking flow to help you prepare accurate customs information for the selected route.
BusinessPage.supportBody: The planned account workspace keeps shipment, document and exception context together; response commitments will be published only after staffing is confirmed.
BusinessPage.requestReceivedBody: Thank you. We have your company details and will review the routes and volume you described.
BusinessPage.contactSubheading: Include the usual route, cargo and frequency. We will use those details to prepare the conversation.

Home.faqSubheading: Everything you need to know about shipping with Nauterio.

faqs.question: How long does international shipping typically take?
faqs.answer: Transit depends on the route and operational acceptance. Air Express typically targets 2-5 business days after export acceptance, Air Economy 5-10 business days, and Ocean Freight follows the confirmed sailing schedule.

faqs.question: Do you help with customs clearance?
faqs.answer: We collect the information needed for the commercial invoice and flag common gaps. If the route needs a broker, permit or additional document, we tell you before accepting the shipment.

faqs.question: Are my shipments insured?
faqs.answer: Protection is not automatically included. If cover is available and requested, its terms and charge must appear in the approved quote or invoice before you rely on it.

faqs.question: Can I track my shipment in real-time?
faqs.answer: The tracking page shows recorded milestones from collection through delivery. Update frequency depends on the carrier and route; it is not a live vehicle map.

faqs.question: What types of goods can you ship?
faqs.answer: We support commercial and personal goods subject to operational review, partner coverage and legal restrictions. If a destination or item needs special handling, operations will confirm before accepting the shipment.

Home.ctaHeading: Tell us about the next shipment
Home.ctaSubtitle: Start with the cargo, origin and destination. We will use those details to check the route and prepare the next step.

SupportWidget.title: Nauterio help
SupportWidget.intro: Quick answers first. Shipment-specific questions go to a person on our team.

quickAnswers.question: Where is my shipment?
quickAnswers.answer: Use the Track page with the complete NT tracking number. If the latest milestone does not make sense, send the number to the support team.

quickAnswers.question: How do I start a shipment?
quickAnswers.answer: Choose Plan a shipment and enter the cargo, dimensions, origin and destination. Nauterio confirms the final rate and collection plan before acceptance.

quickAnswers.question: Which customs documents do I need?
quickAnswers.answer: Goods normally need a commercial invoice with accurate descriptions, values and countries of origin. The exact requirements depend on the route and commodity.

quickAnswers.question: Is shipment protection included?
quickAnswers.answer: No. Protection is optional and applies only when its charge and terms appear in the approved shipment documents.
